div.head: Swer 11
div.ab: Andsæcc. On lifiendes Godes naman, ne ðearf ic N. sceatt ne scylling, ne pænig ne pæniges weorð, ac eal ic him gelæste þæt ðæt ic him scolde, swa forð swa uncre wordgecwydu fyrmest wæron.
In Dei uiuentis nomine, non debeo N. pecuniam uel solidum, nec denarium nec denarii ualens, sed totum ei persolui, quicquid debebam, sicut uerba nostra dicta sunt a principio.
On lifiendes Godes naman, ne ðearf ic N. sceatt ne scylling, ne penig ne peniges weorð, ac eal ic him gelæste ðæt ðæt ic him scolde, swa forð swa uncre wordgecwydu fyrmest wæron.
[I swear] in the name of the living God, [that] I owe N. neither coin nor shilling, penny or pennyworth; but all that I owed I have paid him, just as our initial agreement said.

(Leugnung [dieser Vertragsschuld]. B) Im Namen des lebendigen Gottes, nicht schuld ich dem N. Skat oder Schilling, nicht Pfennig noch Pfennigswerth, sondern all das, was ich ihm schuldete, so weit wie unser beider Verabredung von Anfang an ging, hab ich ihm entrichtet.

(Denial [of this contractual debt]. B) In the name of the living God, I owe N. neither sceat nor shilling, neither penny nor penny's worth, but I have paid him all that I owed him, as far as our agreement went from the beginning.
div.note: Liebermann glosses ‘sceatt’ as the smallest coin. In B two blank lines follow, then A Gu; in H, Að follows after a paragraph break.
